DGGS Terminology Glossary

Source: GLOSSARY.md

Reference for discrete global grid system concepts used in hexify.

Coordinate Systems

PROJTRI (Projected Triangle)

Components: (triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y)

Output of the Snyder forward projection. Each point on Earth maps to a position within one of the 20 icosahedral faces.

Field Range Description
triangle_index 0-19 Which icosahedron face
triangle_x ~[0, 1] Horizontal position within face
triangle_y ~[0, 1] Vertical position within face

Q2DD (Quad 2D Double)

Components: (quad_index, x, y) with floating-point x, y

Intermediate representation after triangle-to-quad conversion. Pairs of adjacent triangles form rhombus-shaped “quads” that allow orthogonal indexing.

Field Range Description
quad_index 0-11 Which quad (pair of triangles)
x, y floating-point Continuous position within quad

Q2DI (Quad 2D Integer)

Components: (quad_index, cell_i, cell_j) with integer indices

Final cell identification at a given resolution. This is the coordinate system DGGRID uses for cell assignment.

Field Range Description
quad_index 0-11 Which quad
cell_i, cell_j 0 to max_coord Integer cell indices

SEQNUM (Sequential Number)

Components: Single integer

Globally unique cell identifier. Useful for database storage and efficient lookups.

Formula: face × cells_per_face + local_index

Icosahedron Geometry

Face

One of the 20 equilateral triangular faces of the icosahedron. Each face has: - A center point (lon/lat) - An azimuth offset for projection alignment - Three vertices shared with adjacent faces

Quad

A pair of adjacent triangular faces forming a rhombus shape. The 20 faces group into 12 quads:

         Quad 0
        (North pole)
       /          \
   Quads 1-5      Quads 6-10
  (Upper band)   (Lower band)
       \          /
        Quad 11
       (South pole)

Quads simplify indexing because rhombuses allow orthogonal (i, j) coordinates while triangles require skewed axes.

Projection

Snyder Equal-Area Projection

Projects the sphere onto icosahedron faces while preserving area. Named after John P. Snyder who developed it.

Direction Input Output
Forward (lon, lat) (triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y)
Inverse (triangle_index, x, y) (lon, lat)

Face Azimuth Offset

Per-face rotation angle that aligns the projection with the icosahedron orientation. Each of the 20 faces has a different offset based on its position.

Variable: face_azimuth_offset (previously dazh)

Newton-Raphson Solver

Iterative algorithm used in the inverse projection to solve for the auxiliary azimuth angle. Converges to ~1e-15 precision in “ultra” mode.

Grid Hierarchy

Aperture

The ratio of cell areas between successive resolution levels. Determines how the grid subdivides.

Aperture Children per Parent Scale Factor Grid Type
3 ~3 √3 ≈ 1.732 ISEA3H
4 4 2 ISEA4H
7 ~7 √7 ≈ 2.646 ISEA7H
Mixed 3/4 varies varies ISEA43H

Resolution (Effective Resolution)

The subdivision level of the grid. Higher resolution = smaller cells = more cells globally.

Resolution Aperture 3 Cells Aperture 4 Cells Approx Cell Area
1 32 42 ~15M km²
5 ~2.6K ~11K ~200K km²
10 ~2M ~11M ~250 km²
15 ~1.5B ~11B ~0.3 km²

Rotation Class

The orientation of hexagons at each resolution level.

Class Orientation Used By
Class 1 Flat-top (vertex up) AP4 always, AP3 even res
Class 2 Pointy-top (edge up) AP3 odd res
Class 3A Intermediate AP7 variant A
Class 3B Intermediate AP7 variant B 
Class 1 (flat-top):     Class 2 (pointy-top):
    ____                     /\
   /    \                   /  \
  /      \                 /    \
  \      /                 \    /
   \____/                   \  /
                             \/

Surrogate Grid

A fine-resolution Class 1 grid used internally to approximate positions in Class 2 or Class 3 grids. The surrogate resolution is typically 2-3 levels finer than the target resolution.

Cell Indexing

Space-Filling Curve

A curve that passes through every cell exactly once, enabling conversion between 2D cell coordinates and 1D indices.

Aperture Curve Type Base Description
3 Z3 Ternary Hierarchical 3-way subdivision
4 Z-order (Morton) Binary Bit-interleaved coordinates
7 Z7 Septenary 7-way subdivision with rotation

Cell Index String

Human-readable cell identifier encoding the hierarchical path from root to cell.

Format: F{face}:{curve}:{digit-sequence}

Example: F5:Z3:1-2-0-1 = Face 5, aperture-3 path [1,2,0,1]

Constants

ISEA Orientation (Default)

Standard orientation matching DGGRID/dggridR: - Vertex 0: lon=11.25°, lat=58.28252559° - Azimuth: 0°

Snyder Constants

From Snyder’s 1992 paper on icosahedral projections: - R1 = 0.9103832815 (scale factor) - SNYDER_G_ANGLE = 36° (icosahedron geometry) - SNYDER_D_ANGLE = 37.37736814° (derived constant)

Earth Geometry

  • Surface area (WGS84): 510,065,621.7 km²
  • Mean radius: 6,371.0088 km

Abbreviations

Abbrev Full Name
DGGS Discrete Global Grid System
ISEA Icosahedral Snyder Equal Area
AP3/4/7 Aperture 3/4/7
Q2DI Quad 2D Integer
Q2DD Quad 2D Double
SEQNUM Sequential Number
